Now I understand the vulnerability clearly. The `lwan_parse_rfc_time` function at line 47 declares `const char in[static 30]`, meaning it expects at least 30 bytes. But the function uses `STRING_SWITCH(str)` which reads 4 bytes via `string_as_int32` without checking the length first. If the `If-Modified-Since` header value is shorter than 30 bytes, it will read past the buffer boundary.

The crash type is "Global-buffer-overflow READ 4" - this is a read past the end of the buffer. The `data_copy` buffer in the fuzz target is 32767 bytes, but the `lwan_value` for the header points into it. The overflow happens when the header value is shorter than 30 bytes and the function reads past the end of the header value.
